newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse up, near new record high.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse up, near new record high.

text.p: German shares ended bourse trade up on Thursday on gains fueled by the overnight advance on Wall Street tied to Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan easing investor concerns about the U.S. market's condition.
The 30-share DAX raced off to a new record high of 3,426.54 points at the start of bourse trade before paring some gains and ended the day up 52.61 points at 3,417.60 points.
The DAX, which has risen more than 200 points in the last two days, was expected to maintain gains in the near-term despite a stunning advance of 200 points in the last two days.
"Greenspan did not give a further warning to the market so Wall Street and the rest of the world can keep going higher," said one Frankfurt trader.
"This is going to be a very strong phase for the German market and it's hard to see an end to the euphoria," he said.
Traders specifically focused on Greenspan's comment that monetary policy was not a tool to "prick stock market bubble", allaying fears of a rate hike to slow the market's advance.
But any sign of weakness in the U.S. market, as well as in the dollar's advance above 1.71 marks, would also certainly trigger a sell-off in Germany, traders said.
"We have coupled ourselves closely to the U.S. and they are in the driver's seat for now," said one trader.

The market generally ignored German jobless data for February, which showed a rise to a seasonally adjusted 4.316 million unemployed, an increase of 5,000, although the data was below market expectations. The jobless rate, which is based on unadjusted data, was unchanged from January at 12.2 percent.

Among specific shares, Kolbenschmidt AG ended up three marks at 29.80 marks after Rheinmetall AG said on Wednesday it took a 24.99 percent stake in Kolbenschmidt in what looked like the prelude to a friendly takeover attempt.
MAN AG ended up 7.50 marks at 477.50 marks on a further advance after investment bank Morgan Stanley added the printing equipment and truck manufacturer to its buy list.

Volkswagen AG reached a new record high at 889 marks before paring gains to end up seven marks at 878 marks after VW chief executive Ferdinand Piech said he saw no indication at the moment of corruption in the carmaker's purchasing department.
VW has so far suspended one employee as part of its probe of allegations of workers demanding and receiving bribes from parts suppliers in exchange for contracts.
